draft.title: Corporate social responsibility in operations
card: Corporate social responsibility (CSR) means a business chooses to act ethically and considers its effect on society and the environment. In operations, this shows in how it sources, makes and delivers its goods or services.
choosing inputs that can be replenished or have a lower impact on the environment, such as timber from certified, managed forests.
reducing the greenhouse gases that production and transport release, for example by running a factory on renewable energy.
paying on time, offering fair prices and giving notice of changes. These count as CSR when they go beyond what the law and contracts require, because the law sets only the minimum.
draft.remember: CSR in operations means choosing to do more than the law requires.

a.q: Which action by a manufacturer is an example of CSR in operations?
opts: Switching its factory to renewable energy to cut emissions
Paying its staff the award wage set by law
Keeping a safety guard on a machine as the law requires
Filing its tax return by the due date
a.why: Cutting emissions by choice goes beyond what the law asks, so it is CSR. The other options only meet legal duties, which is the minimum and not CSR on its own.
a.clue: Which action is a choice rather than a legal duty?

b.q: Lena runs a furniture maker in Geelong. Her contracts let her pay suppliers in 90 days. She now pays small suppliers within 14 days. Why is this CSR in operations?
opts: She treats suppliers fairly, beyond what contracts require
She lowers her own costs by paying suppliers faster
She meets a legal payment deadline set for all suppliers
She cuts emissions from the delivery of her timber
b.why: The contracts allow 90 days, so paying in 14 is a choice that goes beyond the minimum and treats suppliers fairly. No law is described as forcing it, and nothing suggests the faster payment lowers her costs.
b.clue: Compare what the contract allows with what Lena does.

a.best: Switching its factory to renewable energy to cut emissions

b.best: She treats suppliers fairly, beyond what contracts require

check.summary: No problems found. The card correctly frames CSR in operations as going beyond legal and contractual minimums, and both questions have one clearly right answer that matches the explanations.
